title.en: Phrasal Verbs at C1 (bring about, come across, get away with, live up to)
title.es: Phrasal verbs en C1 (bring about, come across, get away with, live up to)

text.en: At C1 level it is no longer the simple everyday phrasal verbs that matter (give up, turn off) but those that express complex ideas compactly: bring about (cause), look into (investigate), come across (find by chance), get away with (escape punishment), make up for (compensate), live up to (meet expectations). Many of them have two or three words and are inseparable. In Spanish they often match a single verb (provocar, investigar, compensar), so learn them together with the meaning.
text.es: En el nivel C1 ya no importan los phrasal verbs cotidianos sencillos (give up, turn off) sino los que expresan ideas complejas de forma compacta: bring about (provocar), look into (investigar), come across (encontrar por casualidad), get away with (salirse con la suya), make up for (compensar), live up to (estar a la altura). Muchos tienen dos o tres palabras y no son separables. En español suelen corresponder a un solo verbo (provocar, investigar, compensar), por eso hay que aprenderlos junto con el significado.

rows: salirse con la suya, sin castigo (phrasal verb)

title.en: Separable: bring about, carry out, point out, work out, sort out
title.es: Separables: bring about, carry out, point out, work out, sort out

text.en: A noun object can go between the parts or after them, a pronoun always between them: bring it about, work it out. Carry out means to perform (an experiment, a plan). Point out means to draw attention to.
text.es: Un objeto nominal puede ir entre las partes o después, un pronombre siempre entre ellas: bring it about, work it out. Carry out significa llevar a cabo (un experimento, un plan). Point out significa señalar.

examples.es: The new law could bring about big changes.

tr.en: The new law could bring about big changes.
tr.es: La nueva ley podría provocar grandes cambios.

examples.es: She pointed out that the date was wrong.

tr.en: She pointed out that the date was wrong.
tr.es: Ella señaló que la fecha estaba mal.

title.en: Inseparable: look into, come across, account for, live up to, make up for, get away with
title.es: No separables: look into, come across, account for, live up to, make up for, get away with

text.en: The object always follows the whole verb, also with a pronoun: look into it, come across it, get away with it. Cut down on and go through with also work like this.
text.es: El objeto siempre va después de todo el verbo, también con pronombre: look into it, come across it, get away with it. Cut down on y go through with también funcionan así.

examples.es: The police will look into the case.

tr.en: The police will look into the case.
tr.es: La policía investigará el caso.

examples.es: He cheated, but he got away with it.

tr.en: He cheated, but he got away with it.
tr.es: Hizo trampa, pero se salió con la suya.

text.en: Account for means to explain or to be responsible for. Live up to is meeting expectations, make up for is compensating.
text.es: Account for significa explicar o ser responsable de algo. Live up to es estar a la altura de las expectativas, make up for es compensar.

examples.es: The movie didn't live up to my expectations.

tr.en: The movie didn't live up to my expectations.
tr.es: La película no estuvo a la altura de mis expectativas.

examples.es: I will make up for the lost time.

tr.en: I will make up for the lost time.
tr.es: Voy a compensar el tiempo perdido.

title.en: Intransitive phrasal verbs: turn out, fall through
title.es: Phrasal verbs sin objeto: turn out, fall through

text.en: Turn out means: it proves that; it is often followed by to be or that: “It turned out to be a mistake.” Fall through means a plan fails.
text.es: Turn out significa: resulta que; a menudo le sigue to be o that: «It turned out to be a mistake.» Fall through significa que un plan fracasa.

examples.es: It turned out to be a mistake.

tr.en: It turned out to be a mistake.
tr.es: Resultó ser un error.

examples.es: The plan fell through because of lack of money.

tr.en: The plan fell through because of lack of money.
tr.es: El plan fracasó por falta de dinero.

title.en: More C1 phrasal verbs: come down with, fall back on, get around to, stand up for
title.es: Más phrasal verbs de C1: come down with, fall back on, get around to, stand up for

text.en: Come down with: to catch an illness. Fall back on: to rely on something when nothing else works. Get around to: to finally find time to do something. Stand up for: to defend someone or something. All of them take an object and cannot be separated.
text.es: Come down with: enfermarse de algo. Fall back on: recurrir a algo cuando nada más funciona. Get around to: encontrar por fin el tiempo para hacer algo. Stand up for: defender a alguien o algo. Todos llevan objeto y no se separan.

examples.es: He came down with the flu last week.

tr.en: He came down with the flu last week.
tr.es: La semana pasada se enfermó de gripe.

examples.es: We can always fall back on our savings.

tr.en: We can always fall back on our savings.
tr.es: Siempre podemos recurrir a nuestros ahorros.

text.en: Play down: to make something seem less important. Buy into: to believe or accept an idea. Clamp down on: to act strictly against something. Rule out: to exclude a possibility. Hold back: to keep back.
text.es: Play down: restarle importancia a algo. Buy into: creerse o aceptar una idea. Clamp down on: actuar con severidad contra algo. Rule out: descartar una posibilidad. Hold back: contener.

examples.es: The minister tried to play down the scandal.

tr.en: The minister tried to play down the scandal.
tr.es: El ministro trató de restarle importancia al escándalo.

examples.es: The doctors cannot rule out a serious illness.

tr.en: The doctors cannot rule out a serious illness.
tr.es: Los médicos no pueden descartar una enfermedad grave.

text.en: With a separable verb a pronoun goes in the middle (bring it about), with an inseparable verb at the end (look into it). Not “look it into” and not “bring about it”.
text.es: Con un verbo separable el pronombre va en medio (bring it about), con uno no separable al final (look into it). No «look it into» ni «bring about it».

text.en: In official texts the one-word verb is often used: investigate, cause, discover, compensate. Phrasal verbs are more natural in speech and less formal.
text.es: En textos oficiales suele usarse el verbo de una palabra: investigate, cause, discover, compensate. Los phrasal verbs son más naturales al hablar y menos formales.

speak.en: At the advanced level the phrasal verbs that express ideas compactly matter. «Bring about» means to cause: «The new law could bring about big changes». «Come across» means to find by chance. «Look into» means to investigate, and it is inseparable: «The police will look into it». «Get away with» means to escape punishment: «He got away with it». «Make up for» compensates, «live up to» meets expectations. «Turn out» means it proves: «It turned out to be a mistake».
speak.es: En el nivel avanzado importan los phrasal verbs que expresan ideas de forma compacta. «Bring about» significa provocar: «The new law could bring about big changes». «Come across» significa encontrar por casualidad. «Look into» significa investigar, y no es separable: «The police will look into it». «Get away with» significa salirse con la suya: «He got away with it». «Make up for» compensa, «live up to» cumple las expectativas. «Turn out» significa resultar: «It turned out to be a mistake».

items.sentence: The new law could ___ about big changes.

take.en: “Take about” does not mean this; you need bring about.
take.es: «Take about» no significa esto; hace falta bring about.

put.en: Put about has another meaning (to spread news); you need bring about.
put.es: Put about tiene otro significado (difundir noticias); hace falta bring about.

tr.en: The new law could bring about big changes.
tr.es: La nueva ley podría traer grandes cambios.

items.sentence: He came ___ with the flu last week.

why.en: Come down with means to catch an illness.
why.es: Come down with significa enfermarse de algo.

up.en: Come up with means to think of an idea; for an illness you need come down with.
up.es: Come up with significa idear algo; para una enfermedad hace falta come down with.

out.en: Come out with means to say something suddenly; for an illness you need come down with.
out.es: Come out with significa soltar algo de pronto; para una enfermedad hace falta come down with.

examples: She came down with a cold.
He came down with a fever.

tr.en: He came down with the flu last week.
tr.es: Él se enfermó de gripe la semana pasada.

items.sentence: I ___ across an old photo while cleaning.

why.en: Come across means to find by chance.
why.es: Come across significa encontrar por casualidad.

went.en: Go across means to cross; you need come across.
went.es: Go across significa cruzar; hace falta come across.

got.en: Get across has another meaning (to communicate an idea); you need come across.
got.es: Get across tiene otro significado (comunicar una idea); hace falta come across.

tr.en: I came across an old photo while cleaning.
tr.es: Me encontré una foto vieja mientras limpiaba.

items.sentence: We can always fall ___ on our savings.

why.en: Fall back on means to rely on something.
why.es: Fall back on significa recurrir a algo.

down.en: Fall down on has another meaning (to fail at something); to rely on something you need fall back on.
down.es: Fall down on tiene otro significado (fallar en algo); para recurrir a algo hace falta fall back on.

out.en: “Fall out on” is not correct in this meaning; you need fall back on.
out.es: «Fall out on» no es correcto en este sentido; hace falta fall back on.

examples: She fell back on her savings.
We have a plan to fall back on.

tr.en: We can always fall back on our savings.
tr.es: Siempre podemos recurrir a nuestros ahorros.

items.sentence: He cheated, but he ___ away with it.

why.en: Get away with means to escape punishment; in the past, got.
why.es: Get away with significa salirse con la suya; en pasado, got.

get.en: Get is not correct in a past sentence; you need got.
get.es: Get no es correcto en una oración pasada; hace falta got.

getting.en: Getting is not a finite verb; you need a finite form (got).
getting.es: Getting no es un verbo conjugado; hace falta una forma conjugada (got).

tr.en: He cheated, but he got away with it.
tr.es: Él hizo trampa, pero se salió con la suya.

items.sentence: I'll ___ up for the lost time by working harder.

why.en: Make up for means to compensate.

do.en: “Do up for” does not exist; you need make up for.
do.es: «Do up for» no existe; hace falta make up for.

take.en: “Take up for” does not mean this; you need make up for.
take.es: «Take up for» no significa esto; hace falta make up for.

examples: He made up for the loss.

tr.en: I'll make up for the lost time by working harder.
tr.es: Compensaré el tiempo perdido trabajando más duro.

items.sentence: The movie didn't ___ up to my expectations.

why.en: Live up to means to meet expectations.
why.es: Live up to significa estar a la altura de las expectativas.

lie.en: “Lie up to” does not exist in this meaning; you need live up to.
lie.es: «Lie up to» no existe en este sentido; hace falta live up to.

leave.en: Leave up to means to let someone else decide; you need live up to.
leave.es: Leave up to significa dejar que otro decida; hace falta live up to.

examples: The food lived up to the hype.

tr.en: The movie didn't live up to my expectations.
tr.es: La película no cumplió con mis expectativas.

items.sentence: I never got ___ to answering that email.

why.en: Get around to means to finally find time for something.
why.es: Get around to significa encontrar por fin el tiempo para algo.

across.en: “Got across to” is not correct in this meaning; you need get around to.
across.es: «Got across to» no es correcto en este sentido; hace falta get around to.

along.en: “Got along to” is not correct; get along with means something else (to be on good terms).
along.es: «Got along to» no es correcto; get along with significa otra cosa (llevarse bien).

examples: I will get around to it soon.
He never got around to calling.

tr.en: I never got around to answering that email.
tr.es: Nunca me di el tiempo de contestar ese correo.

items.sentence: The plan fell ___ because of lack of money.

into.en: Fall into has another meaning (to drop into); you need fall through.
into.es: Fall into tiene otro significado (caer en); hace falta fall through.

at.en: “Fall at” does not exist in this meaning; you need fall through.
at.es: «Fall at» no existe en este sentido; hace falta fall through.

tr.en: The plan fell through because of lack of money.
tr.es: El plan fracasó por falta de dinero.

items.sentence: She will always stand ___ for her friends.

why.en: Stand up for means to defend someone.
why.es: Stand up for significa defender a alguien.

out.en: Stand out has another meaning (to be noticeable); to defend someone you need stand up for.
out.es: Stand out tiene otro significado (destacar); para defender a alguien hace falta stand up for.

by.en: “Stand by for” is not correct here; to defend someone you need stand up for.
by.es: «Stand by for» no es correcto aquí; para defender a alguien hace falta stand up for.

examples: He stood up for his friend.

tr.en: She will always stand up for her friends.
tr.es: Ella siempre defenderá a sus amigos.

items.sentence: The minister tried to ___ down the scandal.

why.en: Play down means to make something seem less important.
why.es: Play down significa restarle importancia a algo.

put.en: “Put down” does not fit a scandal; to make it seem smaller you need play down.
put.es: «Put down» no encaja con un escándalo; para restarle importancia hace falta play down.

turn.en: Turn down means to refuse; for a scandal you need play down.
turn.es: Turn down significa rechazar; con un escándalo hace falta play down.

examples: Do not play down the risk.

tr.en: The minister tried to play down the scandal.
tr.es: El ministro intentó restarle importancia al escándalo.

items.sentence: I do not buy ___ his explanation.

why.en: Buy into means to believe or accept an idea.
why.es: Buy into significa creerse o aceptar una idea.

out.en: Buy out has another meaning (to purchase a share); for an idea you need buy into.
out.es: Buy out tiene otro significado (comprar una parte); para una idea hace falta buy into.

up.en: Buy up has another meaning (to purchase all of something); for an idea you need buy into.
up.es: Buy up tiene otro significado (comprar todo); para una idea hace falta buy into.

examples: Few people buy into this idea.
I do not buy into the hype.

tr.en: I do not buy into his explanation.
tr.es: No me trago su explicación.

items.sentence: How do you ___ for the sudden drop in sales?

count.en: “Count for” does not mean this; you need account for.
count.es: «Count for» no significa esto; hace falta account for.

amount.en: “Amount for” does not exist; you need account for.
amount.es: «Amount for» no existe; hace falta account for.

tr.en: How do you account for the sudden drop in sales?
tr.es: ¿Cómo explica la repentina caída de las ventas?

items.sentence: The police plan to clamp ___ on street crime.

why.en: Clamp down on means to act strictly against something.
why.es: Clamp down on significa actuar con severidad contra algo.

up.en: “Clamp up on” is not correct; you need clamp down on.
up.es: «Clamp up on» no es correcto; hace falta clamp down on.

out.en: “Clamp out on” is not correct; you need clamp down on.
out.es: «Clamp out on» no es correcto; hace falta clamp down on.

examples: The city will clamp down on noise.

tr.en: The police plan to clamp down on street crime.
tr.es: La policía planea tomar medidas contra la delincuencia callejera.

items.sentence: The doctors cannot rule ___ a serious illness.

why.en: Rule out means to exclude a possibility.
why.es: Rule out significa descartar una posibilidad.

off.en: Rule off has another meaning (to draw a line); to exclude something you need rule out.
off.es: Rule off tiene otro significado (trazar una línea); para descartar algo hace falta rule out.

away.en: “Rule away” is not correct; you need rule out.
away.es: «Rule away» no es correcto; hace falta rule out.

tr.en: The doctors cannot rule out a serious illness.
tr.es: Los médicos no pueden descartar una enfermedad grave.

items.sentence: She tried to ___ back her tears.

why.en: Hold back means to keep back.

run.en: Run back means to run in return; you need hold back.
run.es: Run back significa correr de vuelta; hace falta hold back.

sit.en: Sit back means to lean back; you need hold back.
sit.es: Sit back significa recostarse; hace falta hold back.

tr.en: She tried to hold back her tears.
tr.es: Ella trató de contener las lágrimas.

items.sentence: She decided not to ___ through with the wedding.

why.en: Go through with means to carry something through.
why.es: Go through with significa llevar algo hasta el final.

get.en: “Get through with” sounds different (to finish); you need go through with.
get.es: «Get through with» suena distinto (terminar); hace falta go through with.

come.en: “Come through with” does not mean this; you need go through with.
come.es: «Come through with» no significa esto; hace falta go through with.

examples: She will go through with the plan.

tr.en: She decided not to go through with the wedding.
tr.es: Ella decidió no seguir adelante con la boda.
